entries.description: One row per compared run, in input order (duplicates removed).

comparison.description: Deterministic ranking by score, highest first.

TraceReportEntry.description: Per-run row of a benchmark report: aggregated metrics plus derived score.

TraceSummary.description:
Aggregate, deterministic metrics for one run's ordered event sequence.

Every counter is derived purely from event kinds; `elapsed_ms` is the only wall-clock field and is never invented here — a caller with a clock (such as a store query joining recorded timings) may fill it in.

TraceScore.description:
Deterministic comparison score for a [`TraceSummary`].

Each component is per-mille (0..=1000); `total` is therefore 0..=3000.

reliability.description: Completed tasks out of created tasks.

autonomy.description: Resolved attention out of created attention; a run that never needed attention scores full marks.

first_pass.description: Verification passes out of verification attempts.

oneOf.description: Retry cleanup only after the run reaches a terminal state.
Preserve the artifact and record why Loop did not remove it.
A lossy cleanup choice requires an explicit human decision.

FailureClass.description: Infrastructure-neutral classification of an execution or verification failure.

FailurePolicy.description: Deterministic retry decision table. Missing classes fail closed, and deterministic failure classes fail closed even when a budget exists: retry is only ever granted for nondeterministic verification failures ([`FailureClass::is_nondeterministic`]). The deterministic terminal policy — first assertion (or invalid-contract, process-start) failure is terminal — holds regardless of configuration.

RetryBudget.description: Retry budget for one failure class. `max_retries` excludes the initial try.

RetryScope.description: The smallest operation a retry budget permits the executor to repeat.

BackoffPolicy.description: Bounded exponential backoff. A multiplier of one represents fixed backoff.

OnExhaustion.description: What the executor must do when no retry remains.

TerminalizationPolicy.description: Failure propagation rules owned by core rather than an executor adapter.

DependencyTerminalization.description: Terminal state assigned to descendants that require a failed task.

commands.name: recordGuidanceDelivered
commands.description:
Records that a live worker received guidance up to `through_sequence`
(ADR M-TL2 delivery watermark). The store's reducer enforces the
ascending-only watermark per task, so an out-of-order or duplicate
delivery record fails here instead of regressing the projection.

GuidanceDeliveredEvent.description: Wire shape of a steer-mailbox delivery record (ADR M-TL2): the mailbox appends one of these per live worker after a successful `provider.steer`, marking every `GuidanceAdded` at or below `through_sequence` as received by that worker's task. The delivery watermark projection lives in loop-core; this type is only the transport form (see `record_guidance_delivered`).

WorkerState.description:
Lifecycle vocabulary for a worker as observed at the adapter boundary.

This enum is the domain source of the worker-status vocabulary. The bridge carries this type through the optional `state` fields on `WorkerInput` and `WorkerResultInput`, generating the protocol `WorkerState`. These observations do not change the existing worker result policy; absent state remains valid for callers that only report success and summary. Adapters should consume the generated type rather than maintain a copy.

Vocabulary correspondence (decided here, once):

- `starting` / `running` / `completed` / `cancelled` map one-to-one to the adapter session lifecycle. - `lost` is the only terminal-without-result state. An adapter session that ends without a usable result (process exit, API failure, blocked or unobservable agent) reports `lost`; the failure taxonomy and retryability stay adapter-side in the worker result. Recovery uses the same term for a worker that can no longer be observed after a restart.

There is deliberately no `failed` variant: the graph does not distinguish "worker failed" from "worker lost" as a state — both reconcile through the recorded worker result, and the run-level failure vocabulary already lives in [`crate::run::RunState`] and task events.

ComputeCapabilitiesInput.description: Capability scores advertised for a compute candidate (loop-core `ComputeCapabilities` mirror; the core type lacks a JSON schema derive, so the bridge carries its own wire form and converts on entry).

RoutingRisk.description: Task risk driving the compute-class floor (loop-core `Risk` mirror).

payload.title: ConversationAssistantDelta
payload.description: One assistant streaming delta (SSE event `assistant_delta`) for the `message_id` buffer. Gateway-merged (bounded cadence); tokens are never forwarded one-by-one (D4 §2). The final `ConversationAssistantMessage` replaces the whole buffer, so lost or duplicated deltas always converge.

delta.description: Bounded, redacted merged-delta text (append to the buffer).

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the gateway merge.

payload.title: ConversationAssistantMessage
payload.description: The authoritative final assistant message (SSE event `assistant_message`): replaces the entire `message_id` buffer (D4 §2).

truncated.description: True when the final text exceeded the frame byte bound and was cut.

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the tap observation.

payload.title: ContextSummaryEvent
payload.description: Wire shape of one context summarization observation (G1): emitted by the orchestrator when it replaces advisory context with a bounded summary at the task-execution boundary. Preserved sets (completion contract, decision records, failure evidence, guidance) are never summarized, so the record counts them honestly instead of folding them.

attempt.description: Worker attempt the summarized context belonged to.

summarizedEntryCount.description: Advisory entries folded into the summary (activity notes, retry history). Preserved entries are never counted here.

preservedEntryCount.description: Preserved entries passed through untouched (completion contract, decision records, failure evidence, guidance).

summary.description: Bounded, redacted summary text that replaced the folded entries.

truncated.description: True when `summary` exceeded the frame byte bound and was cut.

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the summarization.

ContextSummaryReason.description: Why advisory context was folded into a summary (G1). Variant casing follows the bridge codegen's camelCase rule, so the wire values are `budgetThreshold` / `explicit`.

oneOf.description: The advisory context approached the configured budget threshold and the summarization policy fired (the default trigger).
A lead or operator explicitly requested the summarization.

payload.title: RemoteSessionResetEvent
payload.description: Session stream reset frame (SSE event `conversation_reset`): the convergence contract for cursors, lifetime, and backpressure (decision D3). Connection-local for `cursor_unavailable` / `slow_consumer` (never buffered for replay); `session_gone` is shared-recorded and replayed so reconnects converge identically (pane `paneGone` precedent).

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the gateway observation.

RemoteSessionResetReason.description: Why a session stream converged to a reset frame (decision D3). Variant casing follows the bridge codegen's camelCase rule, so the wire values are `cursorUnavailable` / `sessionGone` / `slowConsumer`. Mirrors the pane family's reset reasons with the session-gone cause named for the session lifetime.

oneOf.description: The presented cursor is malformed, foreign, or points at evicted history; the client restarts from a fresh frame.

The session no longer exists (pi session shutdown); shared-recorded so reconnects converge identically (unlike the other two reasons, this one IS replayed after being recorded — pane `paneGone` precedent).
The connection's outbound queue overflowed; identical in effect to `cursor_unavailable` (fresh start) but named for the cause, connection-local, never buffered for replay.

payload.title: ConversationLifecycle
payload.description: A session/turn lifecycle boundary (SSE event `lifecycle`): the running badge axis. Not a conversation item — never rendered on the timeline (D4 §6).

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the tap observation.

ConversationLifecyclePhase.description:
Lifecycle phase of the observed session (decision D2). Variant casing follows the bridge codegen's camelCase rule, so the wire values are `sessionStarted` / `turnStarted` / `turnEnded` / `sessionEnded`.

Lifecycle frames are a UI axis, not a conversation item: the app uses them for the running badge and never renders them on the timeline (D4 §6).

payload.title: LifecycleHookEvent
payload.description: Typed seam event for adapter lifecycle hooks (G13): the bridge form of one hook observation. Adapters frame these over their own event surfaces; the native bridge never emits or interprets them, and completion checks remain the only completion gate (core judgment invariant).

hookId.description: Adapter-assigned hook identity (its own hook-system name); opaque to the bridge.

runId.description: Correlated run, when the hook ran inside a run-scoped worker.

taskId.description: Correlated task, when the hook ran inside a task-scoped worker.

output.description: Bounded, redacted hook output (formatter logs, policy findings).

truncated.description: True when `output` exceeded the frame byte bound and was cut.

exitCode.description: Hook process exit code, when the hook ran a process.

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the hook observation.

LifecycleHookPhase.description: Which lifecycle boundary fired a hook (G13). The typed vocabulary is fixed at v1; adapters map their own hook systems onto these phases. Variant casing follows the bridge codegen's camelCase rule, so the wire values are `workerStarted` / `workerEnded` / `turnStarted` / `turnEnded` / `toolCallStarted` / `toolCallEnded`.

oneOf.description: A worker process started.
A worker process ended (any terminal state).
A worker turn began.
A worker turn ended.
A tool call began inside a worker turn.
A tool call ended inside a worker turn.

LifecycleHookOutcome.description: Outcome the hook observer reported (G13). Hooks observe; a failed hook is recorded evidence and never overrides run or task state. Variant casing follows the bridge codegen's camelCase rule, so the wire values are `completed` / `failed` / `skipped`.

oneOf.description: The hook ran to completion.
The hook ran and reported a failure (carried as evidence only).
The hook could not run (missing binary, misconfiguration).

payload.title: RemotePaneListOutput
payload.description: GET /v1/panes response body: the pane inventory (decision D4).

RemotePaneSummary.description: One subscribable pane in the terminal-mirror inventory.

label.description: Human label (herdr pane label/title); null when the pane has none.

taskId.description: Loop task id when derivable (e.g. the `mirror·<taskId>` mirror-pane label convention); null when the pane is not task-associated.

RemotePaneState.description: Lifecycle/state vocabulary of an observable pane (decision `2026-xx-terminal-mirror` §6: fixed at M-TM1 from herdr `pane.agent_status_changed` plus gateway-side observation marks). Variant casing follows the bridge codegen's camelCase rule (wire: `active`/`idle`/… single words; multi-word variants camelCase).

oneOf.description: herdr agent_status=working: the pane backs a live agent.
herdr agent_status=idle.
herdr agent_status=blocked.
herdr agent_status=done.
Inventory-only mark: above the gateway's pane observation cap, so no pane stream is served for it (decision D5 upstream bound).
herdr agent_status=unknown (no confident streaming source); apps render this pane as lifecycle-only.

payload.title: RemotePaneResetEvent
payload.description: Pane stream reset frame (SSE event `pane_reset`): carries the pane's latest known snapshot so a client converges without waiting for the next revision change. Connection-local semantics match the run family (ADR §4.5): resets are never buffered for replay.

revision.description: Latest known snapshot counter at reset time; decimal string on the wire.

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the gateway observation.

RemotePaneResetReason.description: Why a pane stream converged to a reset frame (decision D5). Variant casing follows the bridge codegen's camelCase rule, so the wire values are `cursorUnavailable` / `paneGone` / `slowConsumer` (the decision's `cursor_unavailable` / `pane_gone` vocabulary, camelized by codegen).

oneOf.description: The presented cursor is malformed, foreign, or points at evicted history; the client restarts from the latest snapshot.
The pane no longer exists (worker lifetime ended); the stream closes after this frame.
The connection's outbound queue overflowed; identical in effect to `cursor_unavailable` (fresh start from the latest snapshot) but named for the cause, mirroring the run family's `slow_consumer`.

payload.title: RemotePaneTextEvent
payload.description: One pane text frame on `GET /v1/panes/{paneId}/events` (SSE event `pane_text`): the pane's screen-buffer snapshot at `revision`.

revision.description: Monotonic herdr snapshot counter; decimal string on the JSON wire.

text.description: Screen-buffer snapshot text (redacted, UTF-8 bounded by the gateway).

truncated.description: True when the snapshot exceeded the frame byte bound and was cut.

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the gateway observation.

payload.title: SandboxCapabilityReport
payload.description: Inventory of adapter sandbox capability declarations (G4a), mirroring the session/pane list-report shape: one declaration per adapter known to the reporter.

SandboxCapabilityDeclaration.description: One adapter's sandbox capability declaration (G4a): what the adapter can offer, reported by diagnostic surfaces. The declaration is adapter metadata — never loop-core state — and an adapter with no sandbox support declares `isolation: none` rather than omitting itself.

adapterId.description: Adapter-reported identity label (e.g. "codex", "herdr"); opaque to the bridge.

filesystemScoped.description: True when the adapter can confine writes to the declared write scope at the OS level; false means write scope is a scheduler contract only.

networkIsolated.description: True when the adapter can block worker network egress.

detail.description: Bounded human note on the mechanism and its limits; null when the flags say everything the adapter can honestly claim.

SandboxIsolation.description: Honestly-declared OS isolation strength an adapter applies around worker execution (G4a). Variant casing follows the bridge codegen's camelCase rule, so the wire values are `none` / `partial` / `enforced`.

oneOf.description: No OS isolation: worker commands run with the caller's full authority and write scopes are advisory only.
Best-effort isolation (allowlists, policy files, reduced tokens) that a determined process may escape; not a security boundary.
OS-enforced isolation (container, seatbelt profile, restricted token) applied to every worker start.

payload.title: RemoteSessionListOutput
payload.description: GET /v1/sessions response body: the session inventory (decision D3).

RemoteSessionSummary.description: One subscribable session in the conversation inventory (decision D2). The run/task/worker correlation is adapter metadata (env-marker backed), not loop-core state; uncorrelated sessions report nulls honestly.

runId.description: Correlated run, when the worker was started with a run marker.

taskId.description: Correlated task, when the worker was started with a task marker.

workerId.description: Owning worker, when the session backs a registered worker.

lane.description: Execution lane the session runs on (adapter-reported label).

title.description: Human label for list rendering; null when the session has none.

RemoteSessionState.description: Lifecycle/state vocabulary of an observable session (decision D2). Variant casing follows the bridge codegen's camelCase rule, so the wire values are `live` / `ended` / `unobserved`.

oneOf.description: The tap stream is live for this session.
The session ended (`session_shutdown` observed); the stream closes after the shared `session_gone` reset converges.
Known to exist but no tap stream is served for it (honest inventory mark, mirroring the pane family's `unobserved`).

payload.title: ConversationSteerQueued
payload.description: Mirror of an accepted steer on the mapped session's stream (SSE event `steer_queued`): step 2 of the honest 3-step steer feedback (D4 §4 — submit receipt → this frame → the observed `user_message` with `source=steer`). Emitted only for sessions with a run correlation.

steerId.description: Steer acceptance identity; pairs the app's local pending marker.

runId.description: The run the steer was accepted against (adapter correlation).

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the gateway acceptance.

payload.title: ConversationToolCallEnded
payload.description: A tool call ended (SSE event `tool_call_ended`): closes the `tool_call_id` card as `done` or `error` (D4 §3). A card with no prior `started` frame (replay eviction, collector gap) is synthesized closed — never through the `running` state.

resultText.description: Bounded, redacted result text for the card's collapsed view.

resultTruncated.description: True when `result_text` exceeded the frame byte bound and was cut.

isError.description: True renders the card's error state; the run state is unaffected.

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the tap observation.

payload.title: ConversationToolCallStarted
payload.description: A tool call began (SSE event `tool_call_started`): opens the app's tool card in the `running` state (D4 §3).

toolCallId.description: Tap-assigned tool-call identity (pi `toolCallId` correlation); the card's idempotent render key.

argsJson.description: Bounded, redacted JSON encoding of the call arguments.

argsTruncated.description: True when `args_json` exceeded the frame byte bound and was cut.

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the tap observation.

payload.title: UsageRecordEvent
payload.description: Wire shape of one usage observation (G17): emitted by the collecting surface and recorded by the orchestrator. Worker/task correlation is optional so run-level totals use the same record shape.

taskId.description: Worker task the usage belongs to; null for run-level usage.

workerId.description: Adapter worker identity; opaque correlation label.

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the observation window end.

UsageMetadata.description: Optional usage metadata (G17): present only when the upstream reports it. Individual axes are null when unreported; `basis` qualifies every figure in the record at once (adapters do not mix observed and estimated axes).

cacheReadTokens.description: Cache-read tokens when the upstream reports a separate cache axis.

cost.description: Bounded decimal-string cost in `currency`; null when unpriced.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for `cost`; null when unpriced.

UsageBasis.description: How a usage figure was obtained (G17 추정치/실측 구별). Variant casing follows the bridge codegen's camelCase rule, so the wire values are `observed` / `estimated`.

oneOf.description: Upstream-reported actuals.
Locally derived estimate; reporting surfaces must label it as an estimate, never as a measured cost.

payload.title: ConversationUserMessage
payload.description: One user input on the session stream (SSE event `user_message`): a complete user turn as observed by the tap (decision D5, M2).

messageId.description: Tap-assigned message identity; the app's idempotent render key.

imageCount.description: Number of image attachments observed in this input. The honest observed count; `attachments` is the referenceable subset (bodies the gateway actually holds), so it may be smaller (D5).

attachments.description: Reference-shaped attachment metadata. Bodies are served out-of-band at `GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/attachments/{attachmentId}` — never inline (ring-buffer/replay budget, D5).

occurredAt.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp of the tap observation.

ConversationUserMessageSource.description: Channel a user input arrived through, as observed by the in-session tap (decision D2). Variant casing follows the bridge codegen's camelCase rule, so the wire values are `interactive` / `steer` / `api`.

oneOf.description: Normal interactive user turn in the pi session.
Steer injected mid-turn (mailbox drain surfaced in the conversation).
Programmatic input (non-interactive invocation path).

RemoteSessionAssetRef.description: Reference to one attachment body served by the gateway (decision D5, M2): metadata only, never the body. `byte_len` is the DECODED body size in bytes and is bounded far below u32 by the gateway's per-asset cap, so the family stays free of the u64 decimal-string rule.

attachmentId.description: Gateway-assigned attachment identity; addresses the body endpoint.

byteLen.description: Decoded body size in bytes; advisory render metadata (sizing/labels).
